scientific_meaning_and_mechanism: Terrestrial conductive/advective heat transport from mantle/crust to surface
relevance_to_thailand_geology: High: Identifies regional thermal anomalies driving hydrothermal convection
candidate_thai_data_source: IHFC Global Heat Flow Database (Thai borehole records)
availability_in_repository: AVAILABLE (154 records at 111 coordinates across Thailand; 63 records at 50 coordinates in North)
spatial_coverage_status: Extremely sparse point observations; zero continuous coverage
quality_and_uncertainty_limitations: 154/154 records lack measurement uncertainty or error bounds; borehole depth metadata largely missing; severe risk of artifact creation if interpolated
proposed_scientific_transformation: Point observations only; SPATIAL INTERPOLATION FORBIDDEN for predictive raster generation without dense well validation
leakage_and_hallucination_risk: EXTREME: Spatial Kriging/RBF interpolation creates fictional bullseye anomalies around sparse boreholes

scientific_meaning_and_mechanism: Proximity to active/neotectonic extensional or strike-slip faults providing permeability for fluid circulation
relevance_to_thailand_geology: Very High: Northern Thai geothermal systems are fault-controlled extensional basins along Mae Chan / Mae Tha fault systems
availability_in_repository: AVAILABLE (630 line segments in local shapefile)
spatial_coverage_status: Discontinuous line segments; live DMR WFS returns 0 geometries; subsurface 3D dip/geometry unknown
quality_and_uncertainty_limitations: Line generalizations; no subsurface 3D slip rates or hydraulic conductivity; live WFS service unavailable
legal_and_licensing_status: BLOCKED_CONFLICTING_CATALOG_TERMS (Open Government terms conflict with non-commercial metadata; derivative rights unconfirmed)
proposed_scientific_transformation: Euclidean distance transform capped at 30 km with logarithmic/decay scaling
leakage_and_hallucination_risk: HIGH: Using unverified fault traces or missing concealed faults creates false absence bias

scientific_meaning_and_mechanism: Proximity to active/recent volcanic or shallow intrusive magmatic heat engines (<2.6 Ma)
relevance_to_thailand_geology: LOW_TO_MODERATE: Thailand lacks active volcanic arc magmatism; northern granites are Triassic-Cretaceous plutons; Cenozoic basalts (Lampang/Phrae) are intraplate volcanic remnants (~0.6-0.8 Ma)
candidate_thai_data_source: DMR 1:250k Northern Geology (Basalt and Plutonic rock units)
availability_in_repository: AVAILABLE (1266 polygons covering central-north quadrangle extracts)
spatial_coverage_status: 44.74% geometric coverage of candidate AOI; margins missing quadrangle extracts
canonical_processing_unit: Euclidean distance to mapped Neogene/Quaternary volcanic or plutonic contacts in kilometers (km)
quality_and_uncertainty_limitations: Plutons represent deep basement conductive radiogenic sources rather than active magmatic chambers; age dating uncertain for many isolated dikes
legal_and_licensing_status: RESTRICTED_REDISTRIBUTION (DMR terms unverified for derivative map release)
proposed_scientific_transformation: Distance transform to Cenozoic volcanic rocks and radiogenic granite plutons
leakage_and_hallucination_risk: MODERATE: Equating ancient granite batholiths to active Quaternary magma bodies misrepresents thermal mechanism

scientific_meaning_and_mechanism: Microseismicity and earthquake hypocenter clustering indicating active tectonic strain and fracture maintenance
relevance_to_thailand_geology: High: Active micro-earthquakes along strike-slip faults maintain open fractures against mineral sealing/precipitation
candidate_thai_data_source: Thai Meteorological Department (TMD) Earthquake Observation Division Catalog
availability_in_repository: PARTIAL (Historical catalog accessible via public web listings; raw API not integrated)
spatial_coverage_status: National coverage with variable detection threshold (higher sensitivity near seismic stations)
original_measurement_unit: Epicentral coordinates; Richter magnitude (ML/Mw); focal depth (km)
canonical_processing_unit: Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) of hypocenters with M >= 2.0 per km² per decade
quality_and_uncertainty_limitations: Station distribution introduces spatial detection bias (sparse network in remote mountainous areas); focal depth accuracy variable
proposed_scientific_transformation: Spatial Gaussian Kernel Density Estimation with fixed search radius (15 km) and magnitude weighting
leakage_and_hallucination_risk: MODERATE: Station proximity bias must be normalized to prevent attributing seismic network density to geothermal prospectivity

scientific_meaning_and_mechanism: Tectonic stress magnitude and orientation controlling which fault strikes are critically stressed and hydraulically conductive
relevance_to_thailand_geology: High: Faults striking sub-parallel to SHmax (N-S to NNW-SSE in North Thailand) have high dilation tendency and higher fluid permeability
candidate_thai_data_source: World Stress Map (WSM 2016/2019) database / Heidbach et al.
availability_in_repository: PARTIAL (WSM global release accessible; regional focal mechanism stress inversions from published papers)
spatial_coverage_status: Very sparse borehole breakout/drilling data in Thailand; mostly derived from earthquake focal mechanisms
original_measurement_unit: SHmax azimuth (degrees from North); stress regime index (NF/SS/TF)
canonical_processing_unit: Slip tendency and dilation tendency computed from fault strike vs regional SHmax azimuth
quality_and_uncertainty_limitations: Very few in-situ stress measurements in northern inland basins; regional stress orientation generalized across entire Shan-Thai block
proposed_scientific_transformation: Calculation of normalized dilation tendency [Ts = sin²(theta)] for mapped fault segments
leakage_and_hallucination_risk: LOW: Physical tensor calculation based on published geodetic/stress data; requires verified fault strikes
